record_type_quote: In this article, we replicate H&Q's (2014) original work; extend the study to a much larger, comprehensive sample of U.S. stock-listed firms; and analyze the sensitivity of the study's infer- ences to an important change in its method, the use of adjusted R2, and to two important sam- ple characteristics, firm size and CEO tenure.

targets.authors: Hambrick, D. C., & Quigley, T. J.
targets.title: Toward more accurate contextualization of the CEO effect on firm performance.
targets.evidence_quote: In this article, we replicate H&Q's (2014) original work; extend the study to a much larger, comprehensive sample of U.S. stock-listed firms; and analyze the sensitivity of the study's infer- ences to an important change in its method, the use of adjusted R2, and to two important sam- ple characteristics, firm size and CEO tenure.
targets.outcome_quote: We generally confirm H&Q's finding of a high CEO effect, but find a smaller industry effect and a larger firm effect in our larger sample.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors confirm the high CEO effect but explicitly contrast smaller industry and larger firm effects. The confirmation concerns the CEO effect rather than an unqualified verdict on the entire replication.

reasoning: Includes a same-data narrow reproduction and sequential tests in enlarged samples. Coded replication because it retests the published finding in additional firms and years. Only Hambrick and Quigley (2014) is directly retested; other methodological papers provide motivation.
